study type: Retrospective descriptive study from a patient registry
outcome: Diagnosis of Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome (CCHS) of neonatal onset
cohort: The study included 97 infants (44 females) with CCHS of neonatal onset and PHOX2B mutation from 10 European countries.
finding: Polyhydramnios is overrepresented during pregnancy, rapid respiratory failure is the main symptom leading to intubation in approximately half of infants, and daytime alveolar hypoventilation is the main indicator prompting genetic testing for CCHS.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean sections were performed in 30% of pregnancies for infants later diagnosed with neonatal CCHS.
cross-section timing: Data describes events during pregnancy and the first month of life (neonatal onset), with genotype testing confirmed at a median of 32 days post-birth.
